children: Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Health (MOH) and National Centre for Privatisation & PPP (NCP) have launched the request for proposals (RFP) phase for the Chronic Kidney Disease Care & National Dialysis Services public-private partnership (PPP) project.
The RFP was launched on 19 October 2026, following the announcement of 12 prequalified bidders, comprising five consortia and seven individual companies, on 4 October.

The five prequalified consortia are 1) Saudi Arabia’s Care Medical and NephroTech 2) Saudi Arabia’s D.med Healthcare, SMC Hospitals and Al Saedan Real Estate; 3) Germany’s B. Braun and Saudi Arabia’s Gulf Medical Co.; 4) India’s NephroPlus and Saudi Arabia’s Al Faisaliah Healthcare Systems; and 5) China’s WEGO Medical and Saudi Arabia’s ANFAS.

The seven individually prequalified companies are Sweden’s Diaverum, Germany’s NephroCare, Saudi Arabia’s Almana, Saudi Arabia’s Dr. Sulaiman Al Habib Medical Group, US-based U.S. Renal Care, US-based DaVita and UAE-based Burjeel Holdings.
The project forms part of Saudi Arabia's healthcare privatisation and PPP programme.
The authorities did not disclose the RFP submission deadline.
(Writing by SA Kader; Editing by Anoop Menon)
